context: light factory · moulding machines, moulds and cooling water; moulds are the long-lead item

brief.intro: New to this project type? A plastics factory melts plastic pellets and shapes them — by injection into a mould, by blowing into bottles, or by extruding film, sheet or profile. The hall holds rows of machines, each fed with dried pellets through a central vacuum conveying system from silos outside, each needing chilled water to cool the mould, compressed air and a good deal of electricity. Overhead cranes change the heavy moulds. It is one of the simpler factories to build: a clean, flat-floored hall and well-sized utilities. The surprise for newcomers is that the machines are not the long-lead item — the moulds are. Each product needs its own mould, designed, made and tested for that part, and production cannot start until the mould is approved.

scope.name: Site preparation & enabling
scope.desc: Grading, access roads, temporary facilities and underground services.

scope.name: Building & machine foundations
scope.desc: Column footings plus the heavy bases, pits and trenches the machines sit on — set out from the equipment drawings.

scope.name: Steel structure & envelope
scope.desc: Portal frames, crane beams, roof and wall cladding, making the hall weather-tight.

scope.name: Industrial floor
scope.desc: Flat, hard-wearing floor slab, cast after the roof is on and before the machines move in.

scope.name: Resin silos & material handling
scope.desc: Outdoor silos, dryers, blenders and vacuum conveying to the machines.

scope.name: Moulding hall
scope.desc: Injection, blow-moulding or extrusion machines with robots and conveyors.

scope.name: Mould shop & storage
scope.desc: Mould maintenance workshop and racked mould store.

scope.name: Packing & warehouse
scope.desc: Packing lines, palletising and finished-goods storage.

scope.name: Plant utilities
scope.desc: Chilled water & cooling towers, Compressed air, Central material conveying (vacuum), Fire water — the services every machine needs before it can run.

scope.name: Power supply & control
scope.desc: Substation, transformers, switchgear, cabling and the plant control system.

scope.name: Fire protection, HVAC & dust / fume extraction
scope.desc: Life-safety and environmental systems required for the operating permit.

scope.name: Commissioning & ramp-up
scope.desc: Machine acceptance, mould trials, sample approval by the customer for each product, then ramp-up.

must_get_right: Order the moulds first — design, manufacture, trials and corrections take longer than the building and the machines.
Size chilled water, compressed air and power for the full machine list plus growth; these halls are extended often.
The floor must be flat, strong and finished before machines arrive; machine positions also fix the overhead-crane coverage.
Every product needs customer sample approval before production — plan it product by product.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by plant area along the process line and by discipline, with every long-lead machine tracked from order to factory test, shipping and arrival.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar for construction; equipment installation may run extended shifts under vendor supervision. Commissioning follows the vendor's programme, and hot commissioning runs continuously once started.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Foundations and floor → building → cranes → machines set → utilities and material handling → machine acceptance → moulds installed → mould trials → sample approval → production. The critical path runs through the moulds and the customer approvals.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The process technology and vendor are fixed before design starts; vendor drawings for foundations arrive on the agreed dates; permanent power and water are available before cold commissioning; raw material for trial production is on site.

sections.body: The schedule tracks the following as milestones because they drive the programme:

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy machines need crane access and often must enter before the cladding or a wall is closed. Vendor supervisors are booked for fixed periods. Clean, dry, powered conditions are required before precision equipment is unpacked.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: late moulds, repeated mould corrections, undersized utilities, and customer approval cycles. Contingency is held before the first contracted delivery.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by plant area and discipline; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the installation crews and the vendor supervisors — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
